nodes.description: Tbx2 is expressed in non-chamber myocardium of the outflow tract and atrioventricular canal, where it represses chamber differentiation. Tbx2-null mice have atrioventricular canal patterning defects and defective outflow-tract septation, and Tbx2/Tbx3 compound mutants fail to form atrioventricular cushions, the precursors of valves and septa. These requirements match the conotruncal (double outlet right ventricle), septal and valvular defects reported in patients. Heterozygous null mice appear normal, so the patient defects imply that the human missense alleles fall below a dosage threshold the mouse heterozygote does not reach, or interact with other loci.

nodes.description: Patients have congenital vertebral segmentation and fusion defects (Klippel-Feil anomaly, thoracic fusions, hemivertebrae, rib fusions) with secondary scoliosis and kyphosis. TBX2 is expressed in developing bone and cartilage, but no model has shown how reduced TBX2 dosage disrupts somite segmentation or vertebral formation. This node records the human observation; its upstream link to TBX2 rests only on the genotype-phenotype association.

nodes.description: Tbx2 is expressed in palatal shelf mesenchyme. Tbx2-null mice and Tbx2/Tbx3 double heterozygotes have cleft palate because the palatal shelves form but are small, grow slowly and fail to meet, with increased proliferation, apoptosis and Bmp4 and Cyclin D1 expression in the shelves.

evidence.reference_title: Expression and requirement of T-box transcription factors Tbx2 and Tbx3 during secondary palate development in the mouse.
evidence.snippet: Mice homozygous mutant for Tbx2 and mice double heterozygous for Tbx2 and Tbx3 exhibit a cleft palate phenotype arguing for an important contribution of Tbx2 and Tbx3 to palatogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: Expression and requirement of T-box transcription factors Tbx2 and Tbx3 during secondary palate development in the mouse.
evidence.snippet: In Tbx2-deficient embryos, the bilateral primordial palatal shelves form but are smaller and retarded in the outgrowth process. They do not make contact but retain the potential to fuse.

nodes.description: In the mouse, Tbx2 and Tbx3 act redundantly upstream of Tbx1 and hedgehog ligand expression in pharyngeal endoderm, and loss of two of the three genes produces severe pharyngeal hypoplasia. The pharyngeal pouches give rise to the thymus and parathyroid glands, so reduced TBX2 dosage is proposed to produce the DiGeorge-like thymic and parathyroid deficits seen in patients. That the human thymic aplasia arises this way is an inference from the mouse network, not a direct observation.

nodes.description: The thymus fails to form in the p.Arg20Gln family. Because the thymus is the site of T-cell maturation, its absence is the presumed basis of the immune deficiency named in the disorder. The defining report describes Individual 1 as lacking a thymus and functional T cells; numeric T-cell counts are not given in its main text.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants p.Arg20Gln (N-terminal) and p.Arg305His (near the T-box) reduce TBX2 protein levels and its transcriptional repressor activity, and behave as partial loss-of-function (hypomorphic) alleles in Drosophila heterologous expression assays. The disorder is therefore attributed to reduced TBX2 dosage during embryonic development.
